newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton exchange sees selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton exchange sees selective buying.

text.p: European spinning mills made selective purchases of upland cotton and were also seeking extralong- and longstaple qualities, the Bremen Cotton Exchange's fortnightly report said on Monday.
Future weather patterns in the northern hemisphere were still unclear which made crop qualities largely unpredictable, the report said.
Prices were steady to lower in line with recent falls on the New York futures exchange amid bearish fundamentals.
Bremen cotton stocks were reduced by 9,416 bales in the fortnight ended Oct 18 to 42,765 bales, compared with 45,230 bales recorded a year earlier.
In the upland sector, the Exchange reported spot through first half 1997 sales of Central Asian cottons of all standards, Westafricans, Greek high grades, U.S., Zimbabwe and Israel-Acala cotton.

It also reported longstaples sales in Egyption Giza 77 and 75/86 grades as well as U.S.-Pima for fourth quarter 1996 and first quarter 1997, while Israel-Pima sales also stretched into second quarter 1997.
The Exchange reported ex-stocks spot sales of California/Arizona origin but added demand for Central Asian higher grades could not be satisfied.
